subject: Acme - TCO post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - TCO post-call recap and next steps

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our conversation plus next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: inference costs are spiking as Acme scales chat assistants (high qps, many short-lived sessions). You called out expensive repeated prompt prefixes and heavy tail of completion tokens per session.
- Goal: get to predictable, < $X per active user/month TCO while keeping latency under 300ms p95 for web chat and preserving LLM quality for core intents.

Key constraints we captured
- Budget guardrail: $60k/month for model inference initially (pilot).
- Expected traffic profile: 2M requests/month, median prompt 220 tokens, median response 110 tokens, 15% long tail (>1k tokens). Sample usage attached (acme_sample_usage.csv).

Redwood recommendations (cost levers) — high level
1) Token economics & model selection:
   - Recommend r-instruct-3b-q4 (quantized) for broad intents; r-sync-7b for high-value intents where quality matters.
   - Estimated nominal token pricing (hosted API, committed dedicated pricing shown in sheet): prompt tokens: $0.0004 / 1k tokens; completion tokens: $0.0012 / 1k tokens.
2) Batching & latency tradeoffs:
   - Use request coalescing with 10-20ms queuing window for background tasks (reduces per-token cost by ~18% in our sims).
3) KV prefix caching for system prompts/persistent context:
   - Cache common prefixes per session to cut repeated prompt tokens by ~40% for chat flows.
4) Quantization & model variant routing:
   - Route low-critical queries to quantized 3b; route payoffs to 7b. Automatic fallback maintains availability.

Estimated pilot cost (monthly, rough) — see attached spreadsheet for details
- Conservative: $48k/mo (with batching + prefix caching, 30% quantized usage)
- Baseline: $72k/mo (no batching/caching; all requests to 7b-class)
- Recommended pilot target: $55k/mo (blend + latency SLO)

Next steps / asks
- Marissa (me): I will share the TCO workbook (redwood_tco_acme_v1.xlsx) with 3 scenarios and a short ROI slide.
- Alex: confirm whether the 15% long-tail sessions are eligible for a separate higher-latency workflow (we discussed offline async processing).
- Procurement/finance: if pilot budget looks OK, Rafael will engage to outline committed capacity options and a contract draft.

Attachments: redwood_tco_acme_v1.xlsx, acme_sample_usage.csv

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 30m call to walk through the workbook.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before I share with finance/procurement:

1) Can you translate the "prompt vs completion token" pricing into an expected cost per 1M requests for the conservative and recommended pilot scenarios?
2) For the KV prefix caching — any changes required on our side (SDK changes, session management)?
3) Do you have a brief ROI example for a single product team (e.g., 5k daily active users) to show cost vs. incremental revenue retention?

Procurement will want to see committed vs on-demand delta and what the minimum commitment looks like. Also cc'ing Jordan from our procurement team (looping him in).

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - TCO post-call recap and next steps

Alex — great questions. See quick answers below and attached workbook has per-scenario breakout. I also added a 1-pager ROI slide in the Drive link.

1) Cost per 1M requests (approx, using your median token profile: prompt 220, completion 110)
   - Conservative scenario (high 7b usage): ~1M reqs = 330M tokens => ~$396 (prompt) + ~$396 (completion at higher rate) = ~$792 per 1M requests in baseline.
   - Recommended (mix, 30% quantized): ~1M reqs = 330M tokens but 30% at quantized pricing -> ~ $640 per 1M requests.
   - Note: batching gains and KV caching reduce billed prompt tokens; applied in the workbook as a 25-35% token reduction depending on flow.

2) KV prefix caching — engineering effort
   - Minimal SDK changes: we provide a small client helper that registers per-session prefixes and retrieves a cache key. Server-side supports prefix keys out of the box. Should be ~1-2 sprints to instrument across chat flows. Rafael can share an implementation guide.

3) ROI example (high level) — 5k DAU product team
   - Assumptions: 5k DAU, 3 requests/user/day = 15k requests/day -> ~450k req/month. Using recommended mix -> ~450k * $0.64k per 1k ~= $288/mo in inference (normalized). Example retention lift + unit economics shown in attached slide (conservative uplift 1.5% retention -> incremental ARR ~ $45k/yr for that product team).

Commitment vs on-demand:
- Typical committed discount: 20-35% depending on term and committed capacity. We can model a 12-month commit that targets your pilot usage to stabilize unit price. Rafael — can you drop proposed commitment tiers and a sample contract outline?

I've attached redwood_tco_acme_v1.xlsx and the usage sample for your team to review. Linking the Drive copy: https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme/tco-v1 (editable to fill your numbers).

If that looks good I can book a 30m run-through with your team early next week.

Best,
Marissa
